items.title: Harry "Sweets" Edison interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: Count Basie introduced me to Ellington, James P. Johnson, Art Tatum, Louis Armstrong, oh my goodness.

ctx.x: I couldn’t miss it. I couldn’t go to bed. I lived on 130th and Seventh Avenue. Art Tatum was playing on 131st Street, Don Redmond was playing across the street at 132nd Street, Billie Holiday was singing at 138th Street at a place called the Yeah Man Club, there was Small’s Paradise on 135th Street. Everything was in Harlem. You know you could walk, and I walked so much ‘till I just passed out. I just couldn’t miss anything. So everybody was, you could see everybody that you wanted to see in the daytime on…

Club. It was just, it was amazing and it held my, I was just in awe at all of these people that I had seen on the stage in Columbus, Ohio at a dance. Cab Calloway. Here I am walking down Seventh Avenue, and looking at these people and saying hello to them. And Count Basie introduced me to all these people. He was like a father. When I first joined the band I was 19 and he just took a liking to me and he introduced me to Ellington, James P. Johnson, Art Tatum, Louis Armstrong, oh my goodness. It was just…

items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: But I only met him in Cleveland, never met him in Toledo.

ctx.x: And how did Roy’s playing strike you in contrasting it with Louis?

Oh, he was exciting, there’s no doubt about it. He never did get tired. I played ‘til 4:00 in the morning on my gig and there was after hour places there where you could go play, and he would play until 10, 11, 12, 1:00 in the daytime. Then we’d go over and hear Art Tatum play. Art Tatum was playing at a place called Val’s in the Alley in Cleveland after he left Toledo. And we’d all go over there and listen to him if you could get in the place cause the place he played was about as big as this apartment here. And…
Did you get to jam with him much there or play with him?

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: And that's the first time I met Art Tatum. He was playing at a club around there called Valson (PHONETIC) Alley in Cleveland.

ctx.x: Yes, I know that. I was wondering why -- you know, I always thought of Crawford as playing in Memphis but I knew Sy came from up there.

He's from Zanesville. And the Mills Brothers are from Pickaway, Ohio. They're from Ohio. Earl Warren is from Ohio. Teddy Wilson spent a lot of time in Ohio with Speed Webb, he was from Ohio. Chick Carter, Snooky Young's old boss, he's from Ohio. Art Tatum was from Toledo. There are many, many good musicians from Ohio. Eli Robertson, the trombone player, he was from around Ohio.
But see, all those bands used to station themselves in Ohio, Columbus, because they could go to Cincinnati, only 90 miles, go to Steubenville, only 60 miles.
